semantic_content.answer: No. The argument is a contradiction proof: assuming a lowest-terms rational representation leads to both numerator and denominator being even, contradicting lowest terms. Thus the claim that sqrt(2) is rational is false; sqrt(2) is irrational. The inference that a and b are even is valid when the parity implication “if n² is even, then n is even” is supplied, as done below.
